header:
Date: 2025-03-29
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Sara (Redwood Solutions), Ethan (CTO, Strata), Priya (Backend), Liam (Product)
summary: Introductory hosted API walkthrough focused on streaming behavior, tuning generation params (temperature/top_p/max_tokens) and retry/backoff strategies. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a conversational triage product. Security/SLOs and latency percentiles are primary concerns.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya at redwood inference. quick intro from our side, jonah is the se, sara will hit console stuff.
[00:18] Ethan: thanks, yeah from strata, im ethan, we run a symptom triage chat for clinics, latency is a big deal for us, also sensitive pII.
[00:34] Maya: totally makes sense, today we'll demo the hosted chat sandbox, show streaming, param effects, and cover retry patterns you can use in prod. we'll also point to the console and optimize suggestions.
[00:52] Jonah: i'll start with a live sandbox curl, it's a single endpoint for chat generation, streaming will chunk tokens. watch the latency and how we send incremental events.
[01:12] Speaker 1: (background) okay go ahead,
[01:22] Jonah: "curl -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat ..." and we set a low max_tokens and temperature 0.2 for concise answers.
[01:37] Priya: quick q: how does streaming affect perceived latency vs full response? we care about first-byte time.
[01:50] Jonah: streaming returns tokens as they're generated so first-byte is when token 1 appears; you can tune model choice + max_new_tokens and also set early_stop heuristics in client to return after certain token patterns.
[02:10] Maya: also we default to small prefix caching for repeated prompts which helps p50. for your triage flows, repeated system prompts are a win.
[02:26] Liam: when would you recommend hosted vs dedicated? cost is a concern and we may scale fast.
[02:36] Maya: hosted is fastest to get going and we have curated open models with performance profiles. dedicated gives predictable throughput, reserved GPUs, and isolation. for Strata if you need strict data residency or on-prem, Private is an option.
[02:55] Ethan: what about encryption and logs? we need audit trails and key management.
[03:05] Sara: we support KMS integrations, audit logs, SAML SSO and SOC 2. we'll share the security one-pager.
[03:18] Priya: ok perf question: how do retries interact with idempotency? if a request times out at client but maybe succeeded server-side.
[03:30] Jonah: good one. we recommend idempotency keys for non-streaming batch calls; for streaming you can add a request id and a small reconciliation window. client-side exponential backoff with jitter is the pattern — start with 200ms-500ms then double, max 4 retries typically.
[03:54] Ethan: you said kv cache earlier — is that the key/value attention cache? does it persist across requests?
[04:05] Maya: it's prefix/KV cache: short-term cache for repeated prefixes in the same session. it doesn't persist indefinitely unless you wire in a reuse pattern. helps with cost for repeated context.
[04:22] Priya: could we see token accounting in the console? need to map cost to user sessions.
[04:31] Sara: yes console has token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards, you can see model, tokens, and cost. also Optimize will suggest batching and quantization options for cost.
[04:48] Jonah: demoing a latency vs throughput trade: i switch model to a smaller quantized variant, see lower p50 but slightly degraded turn-by-turn quality.
[05:02] Priya: uh can you repeat that model name? the transcript garbled earlier —
[05:08] Jonah: sorry, it's the redwood-7b-q4f model in the catalog, we surface perf numbers in the model card.
[05:18] Ethan: our SLO is p95 < 600ms for first token, is that realistic?
[05:27] Jonah: depends on request size and model. with smaller models and local region routing it's achievable; hosted can meet that p95 for short prompts, otherwise dedicated with reserved GPU gives tighter control. we'd want to run a short benchmark.
[05:45] Maya: action: we'll scope a benchmark (jonah) with your sample prompts and measure p50/p95/p99, link in ticket.
[05:54] Speaker 2: (overlap) also retry logic can cause bursts, consider circuit breaker on client.
[06:05] Priya: do you have libraries for retries and idempotency?
[06:12] Jonah: yep we have example client code with backoff and idempotency key patterns in the SDK and docs.
[06:22] Maya: let's walk console: sara, can you share your screen? (screen share noise)
[06:30] Sara: here is the console, route-level dashboards, you can pin model versions and set canary rollouts. here's the logs: you can filter by token and trace id.
[06:52] Priya: nice, can we set auto-fallback to cheaper model under high-latency?
[06:58] Sara: yes routing policies support fallback chains: region, cost-tier, model variant. you get golden path for latency and fallback to cost-saver.
[07:12] Ethan: curious about batching: could batching increase latency for single-user chat?
[07:19] Jonah: batching is workload dependent. for single interactive sessions you want low batch windows; we use dynamic batching and concurrency knobs. Optimize suggests batching thresholds where it helps cost without violating latency SLOs.
[07:37] Priya: what about rate limits and quota spikes?
[07:42] Maya: hosted has rate limits, and you can request quota increases; Dedicated avoids noisy neighbor issues.
[07:52] Liam: any gotchas with streaming reconnects? like partial events and resuming from kv cache.
[07:59] Jonah: reconnects can be resumed by storing last token index and replaying recent context; sometimes last chunk duplication occurs, clients should dedupe by token index or id.
[08:16] Priya: do you support delta updates vs full message payloads?
[08:22] Sara: streaming is delta by token, but for webhook-style sinks you can choose full vs partial messages.
[08:32] Ethan: could we get a short checklist for production: retry thresholds, idempotency policy, circuit breakers, and SDK config?
[08:40] Maya: yes we'll send a simple runbook and sample SDK config.
[08:46] Jonah: i'll attach a curl repro and a small benchmark plan.
[08:51] Priya: timeline: we'd like to validate within 2 weeks and then decide on hosted pilot.
[08:58] Maya: sounds good — we'll aim for a benchmark in the next week.
[09:04] Liam: any competitor considerations? we're also evaluating openai and anthropic for model quality.
[09:12] Maya: noted — we'll include model quality vs latency trade slides and a short comparison.
[09:18] (cross talk)
[09:30] Maya: recap: 1) Maya to share security docs and pricing; 2) Jonah to run benchmark and share repro; 3) Priya to send sample prompts and SLOs. schedule tech deep dive next week.
[09:47] Ethan: thanks all, that was useful.
[09:51] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.
[09:55] (meeting ends)
